operations.specification:
Registration endpoint for new user creation. This operation enables an individual to sign up for the Todo List application by providing a unique email address and a password. It is associated with the 'todo_list_users' Prisma table, which stores each user's credentials and identity. The API validates both the uniqueness of the email (enforced in the schema's unique index) and the adequacy of the password, hashing it for secure storage in the 'password_hash' column. Upon successful registration, a record is created in the database and JWT tokens (access and refresh) are issued directly to the newly registered user.

Security is enforced by never exposing sensitive information (e.g., raw password) and by requiring minimum password criteria as detailed in the business requirements. The user is the sole actor—no guest registration, admin paths, or cross-account references exist. Only the email and password are accepted; excess fields are rejected. If the provided email already exists, a clear error is returned—users cannot overwrite or hijack other accounts.

Like all authentication flows, this endpoint is deliberately public (authorizationActor: null). It integrates tightly with the user-session establishment: registration both creates the user record and generates a valid session. All fields referenced in input/output map directly to the schema; no derived settings are inferred.

Related endpoints: login (for subsequent authentications), refresh (for token renewal), and logout (for session invalidation) complete the core flows. Credentials provided here are stored only as irreversible secure hashes, as mandated by the schema and requirements.

In all normal and error paths, no internal implementation details are ever leaked. Response always provides fresh JWT tokens for use in secure API calls immediately following registration.
operations.description: Registers a new user in the system and issues authentication tokens. Tied to todo_list_users table. Validates unique email and hashes password as per schema.
operations.summary: Register a new user account in todo_list_users and issue tokens.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials: email and password. Email must be unique. Password will be hashed as per security rules.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens (access/refresh) and userId for newly registered user, as per application conventions.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
Credential-based authentication endpoint for issuing JWT tokens. Authenticates a registered user using email and password, leveraging the 'todo_list_users' Prisma table and unique index on email. On valid credentials, a new session record is created in 'todo_list_user_sessions' with device/ip metadata as described in the session-table schema; session lifecycle is fully auditable.

The operation receives an email and password, verifies the email exists, and matches the password against the securely hashed value in 'password_hash'. No raw passwords are stored or returned. On success, access and refresh tokens are issued. If the email does not exist or credentials are wrong, a secure error is returned without revealing field-specific failure.

This endpoint is strictly public for credential validation. It does not support login via username, phone, or social accounts; only email and password are accepted. It creates a session entry (including ip, href, and referrer) using fields in the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table; audit info is available for security monitoring.

Related endpoints: join (initial registration), refresh (token rotation), and logout (session invalidation). No cross-user/admin login is permitted or supported in this minimal system.

All error and success flows comply with user privacy guidelines: detailed cause is logged but not exposed to end user. Tokens are returned only for successful authentication events.
operations.description: Authenticates a user with email and password. On success, creates a new session in todo_list_user_sessions and issues JWT tokens. References todo_list_users for credential verification and session management.
operations.summary: Authenticate user via email/password (todo_list_users); issue tokens and log session to todo_list_user_sessions.

requestBody.description: Login credentials: email and password of existing user, as persisted in todo_list_users.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens (access/refresh) and userId for authenticated user, conforming to authorization contract.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
JWT token refresh endpoint for extending authenticated access. Allows a user to exchange a valid (unexpired, non-revoked) refresh token for a new set of access/refresh tokens. Relies on the user's identity as persisted in 'todo_list_users' and the session lifecycle as tracked in 'todo_list_user_sessions'.

The refresh token is presented for validation; if valid, a new session record may be created and old tokens rotated/invalidated. If the refresh token is expired, tampered, or not issued by this service, a business-specific error is returned. The session's audit trail (ip, href, referrer, expiry) ensures full traceability—fields strictly follow the session schema and requirements.

This operation does not require credentials or expose any user data—just a valid refresh token (per secure httpOnly cookie or header per business rules). It always returns new tokens and associated identity payload; on failure, only a generic error is issued. User cannot refresh tokens for any actor or session other than their own.

Closely related to login (for session start) and logout (for session end). No admin-level or bulk token operations exist; each refresh is for the authenticated user's one session.

Security: ensures all tokens and session records mapped to the authenticated user, in strict alignment with the business requirement of preventing cross-user access.
operations.description: Refreshes a user's authentication tokens (access and refresh) using a valid refresh token, as tracked in todo_list_users and todo_list_user_sessions. Audits session per schema fields.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for a user session (todo_list_users, todo_list_user_sessions).

requestBody.description: Valid refresh token, provided per secure transport policy. No other parameters accepted.

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens (access/refresh) for the user, as per schema/spec.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification:
Logout endpoint to immediately invalidate a user's active session, revoking issued access and refresh JWT tokens for that session. References the current session (as persisted in todo_list_user_sessions), and deletes the relevant session record. Session conclusion is tracked using the 'expired_at' field in the session schema—on logout, timestamp is set.

This endpoint is strictly for session invalidation: once called, both access and refresh tokens for this session are rendered unusable and cannot be exchanged or replayed. The 'todo_list_users' and 'todo_list_user_sessions' Prisma tables underpin this process, ensuring business and security requirements are met—user cannot log out other users, and no tokens outside the user's session are impacted.

User is required to be authenticated (authorizationActor: 'user'). There is no need for a request body; the session is determined by the current authentication context (the JWT or session id). Logout is audited for security: session expiry and user id, with 'expired_at' timestamp recorded for event traceability.

Related endpoints: login (session start), refresh (token rotation), join (new account creation). No admin/guest/session transfer flows are supported.
operations.description: Logs out the authenticated user by invalidating their active session in todo_list_user_sessions (expiry set), revoking all JWT tokens for this session. Only affects the current user's session context.
operations.summary: Logout current user and invalidate their session (todo_list_user_sessions).

responseBody.description: Session termination confirmation; no additional data returned.

operations.name: logout

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the authenticated user's own account profile based on their email-identified user record in the 'todo_list_users' Prisma table. It enables a logged-in user to view their personal profile, including email and account creation timestamp, without exposing credential hashes or system-internal identifiers. No path parameters are required. Actor is always the user themselves, not arbitrary lookup.
operations.description:
Retrieve the currently authenticated user's profile information.

This operation allows a logged-in user to view their own account details, including their email address and the date they registered. The response omits sensitive fields such as password hashes and internal record IDs, ensuring that confidential credential data remains secure.

Access is restricted to authenticated users; the endpoint never exposes data for other users or permits administrative overrides. The operation integrates session authentication to confirm the user's identity. Its logic is based on the 'todo_list_users' Prisma table, referencing the unique email-based business identifier.

This endpoint forms the primary method by which application users access their own profile. Account modification requires the dedicated PUT operation on the same path. Rate-limiting and audit logging should be considered for security best practices.
operations.summary: View the authenticated user's own profile from the todo_list_users table.

responseBody.description: Authenticated user's profile information without sensitive credential details.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates the profile of the authenticated user in the 'todo_list_users' table. It enables users to modify their account data, such as updating their email or password. The update is performed strictly on the user's own record, identified by authentication context; path parameters are not required. Email remains the unique business identifier and cannot be set to an address already used by another account. Updates are subject to validation and constraints as described in the Prisma schema.
operations.description:
Update the currently authenticated user's account profile.

This operation allows a logged-in user to modify their own profile details, such as changing their email address or password. All updates are subject to validation rules consistent with the 'todo_list_users' Prisma table: the email must remain unique across the system, and the password is stored as a secure hash. Attempts to update to a duplicate email or provide an invalid password will result in errors as defined by the business rules.

Only the authenticated user's own record can be updated by this endpoint. Administrative changes to other accounts are not possible through this operation. Password changes require providing a hash of the new password; plain text passwords are never accepted or returned. After a successful update, the response returns the updated profile information, excluding credential hashes or internal-only fields. Audit logging and security policies apply to profile update actions.
operations.summary: Update the authenticated user's profile in the todo_list_users table.

requestBody.description: Updated profile data for the authenticated user (email, password, etc.), subject to validation and constraints.

responseBody.description: Updated authenticated user's profile, omitting sensitive password hashes.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes the authenticated user's account from the todo_list_users table. It accepts only authenticated requests, ensuring the operation is restricted to the current user (self-service paradigm). User account information—email and password hash—is deleted alongside all related business data, including all personal todo items (from todo_list_todos) and all session records (from todo_list_user_sessions). No soft delete or delayed removal is used as per explicit business requirements. Deletion is immediate and irreversible, enforcing true user data removal per privacy mandates. All cascade actions and removals of foreign-key dependent entities, such as the user's todos and sessions, are handled at the database or provider level based on strict referential integrity constraints.
operations.description:
Permanently and irreversibly deletes the authenticated user's account from the system. Upon invocation, this endpoint ensures the authenticated user is identified through secure session or token context, allowing only the user themselves to initiate the deletion.

All associated data, including todo items (each record in todo_list_todos owned by the user) and session records (from todo_list_user_sessions), are also removed as part of a comprehensive, cascading deletion policy. This supports both privacy and data minimization requirements, fulfilling expectations for user-driven account destruction.

Security is paramount: the endpoint validates user identity and enforces that no other user or administrator can delete accounts on behalf of someone else. Strict auditing and referential checks are applied. Related operations include creating a user, modifying account details, or logging out—all of which become invalid after this deletion. 

The operation is guided by the requirement that no soft deletion occurs, no restoration is possible, and all deletions are performed immediately and without retention.
operations.summary: Permanently delete the authenticated user's account from the todo_list_users table.
operations.name: erase

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of session records for the authenticated user from the todo_list_user_sessions table. The endpoint enables comprehensive searching and audit access to a user's own concurrent sessions, as tracked by the 'todo_list_user_sessions' model. Query support includes filtering by activity status, originating IP, session URL, referrer, and time ranges. This supports privacy audits, device management, and suspicious session checks. Session modification or invalidation is not exposed via this endpoint. Only authenticated users may make requests; no public or admin session-overview is supported by business requirements.

Response structure aligns with the ITodoListUserSession.ISummary interface, providing minimal but sufficient session metadata for enumeration and overview.
operations.description:
Searches and lists all session records for the currently authenticated user, supporting advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting options. The endpoint gives users visibility into their login activity over all devices and browsers via the todo_list_user_sessions table.

Session records can be filtered by activity (active/expired), connection metadata (IP, origin URL, referrer), and time-range criteria. The response contains session summaries, exposing only essential metadata (timestamps, IPs, URLs) for privacy and account management.

The operation is strictly read-only: users cannot create, modify, or delete sessions directly through this endpoint. Invalidation of sessions (such as logout from all devices) is handled by the authentication subsystem and not via business application APIs. Only the user themselves may invoke this operation; no administrative listing or cross-user queries are supported.

This operation prevents arbitrary access, safeguards user privacy, and supports best practices for session enumeration and monitoring.
operations.summary: Search and enumerate session records for the authenticated user (todo_list_user_sessions).

requestBody.description: Complex search, filtering, and pagination criteria to enumerate user session records.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session summary objects for the current user's sessions.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific session belonging to the authenticated user. It is based on the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table in the Prisma schema, which stores records of user login sessions, including the session's origin, creation, and expiration times. The operation requires the sessionId path parameter, referencing the session's unique identifier. It is restricted so that only the owner of the session (the currently authenticated user) can access their own session details. All relevant fields from the 'todo_list_user_sessions' model are included in the response for auditability.
operations.description:
Fetch a specific session's details for the authenticated user.

This endpoint allows users to view the details of one of their active or historical sessions, which may include login timestamp, device/network info, referrer, and session expiration time. Only the user who owns the session may retrieve its details; there is no public or administrative access to session records from this endpoint.

The session data provides auditability and transparency to account holders, helping detect unauthorized access or monitor recent activity. All session model fields, such as IP, href, referrer, and timestamps, are available in the response.

Access errors will occur if the sessionId does not belong to the current user or does not exist.
operations.summary: Retrieve the details of an authenticated user's session based on sessionId (todo_list_user_sessions).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session record belonging to the current user.

responseBody.description: Detailed session information record owned by the authenticated user.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation deletes (immediately invalidates) a specific session for the currently authenticated user by removing the corresponding record in the 'todo_list_user_sessions' Prisma table. It is a self-service operation, allowing users to manually log out from any of their active sessions, such as for account security after device loss. Only the owner can erase their sessions; there is no administrative or third-party actor access. The session is permanently removed—no soft deletion applies.
operations.description:
Terminate and remove a user's session by sessionId.

The DELETE endpoint allows a logged-in user to invalidate one of their current or past sessions. Deleting a session immediately logs it out and removes its audit record, helping users secure their accounts if they suspect unauthorized activity.

This operation is self-service and only applicable to the current user's own sessions. Administrative or cross-user session deletion is not exposed. Permanent deletion is performed, with no recovery for removed session data.
operations.summary: Erase an authenticated user's session by sessionId (todo_list_user_sessions).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the session record belonging to the current user.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered and paginated list of todo items that belong exclusively to the authenticated user, using the todo_list_todos Prisma table. Search, filtering, and sorting is performed on key fields such as completion status, creation date, title, and completion date. The operation supports efficient per-user data isolation by enforcing user-specific queries based on the foreign key relation to todo_list_users. Only authenticated users may access their own todos; cross-user access is prohibited by business mandate. The operation's DTO and field references precisely match the todo_list_todos schema, supporting extensible validation and prevents access to deleted or orphaned data by omitting soft-deleted handling, since the schema is designed for hard deletion only.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated, filterable list of todo items owned by the authenticated user. This endpoint enforces strict user-level data partitioning, ensuring that each user can only access their own tasks as per the foreign key constraint to todo_list_users. Advanced filtering includes support for searching on title, completion status, creation and completion timestamps, and partial or case-insensitive text search where appropriate.

The operation is designed for high performance with user-specific queries and supports business workflow requirements for quick viewing, filtering, and management of personal tasks. All responses are scoped: users only ever see their own data. Pagination and sort options on creation date and completion status provide flexibility for user-facing clients, and the response returns summary representations for optimal list rendering.

Authorization is enforced at the application layer; the server only returns rows for the authenticated user extracted from the session. No administrator, moderator, or cross-user search is permitted. This operation does not display soft-deleted results, as all deletions are permanent according to strict business requirements.
operations.summary: Search, filter, and paginate the authenticated user's todo_list_todos records.

requestBody.description: Criteria for searching and paginating a user's todo items, including filters for completion status, creation timestamps, and free-text search on title or description.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of summary views of user's todos, matching the search and filter criteria provided, suitable for overview displays.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a single todo item by its unique identifier, but only if the requested todo is owned by the authenticated user, using todo_list_todos as the authoritative data source. The operation's purpose is to provide detailed information for one not-deleted, per-user task with strong data partitioning enforced by both path parameter and business logic. The todo_id field in the path must be a valid UUID and correspond to an owned todo; requests for non-owned or non-existent todos will result in 'not found' errors, preserving strict privacy and data integrity.
operations.description:
Retrieve all detailed information for an individual todo managed by the authenticated user. The operation is protected so that only the recorded owner, matched on user_id, may access this resource; unauthorized access or attempts to fetch non-existent/other-user todos return not found responses, supporting both security and data privacy.

This endpoint aligns request and resource identities using the permanent, non-recycled UUID from the database. Details returned include the required title, optional description, current completion status and timestamp, audit fields such as created_at and updated_at, and user ownership context (never exposing unrelated user records).

Field validations, error handling, and access control are consistently enforced following the core business requirements from both the requirements document and strict Prisma schema constraints. No unrelated user or system actors are permitted; only self-service for the authenticated user identity is supported by this operation.
operations.summary: Get a detailed todo_list_todos record by its ID for the authenticated user.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier UUID of the todo item to retrieve (must be owned by the requesting user).

responseBody.description: Full detail for one todo item, including all business-critical and audit fields, if and only if owned by the authenticated user.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created first before it can be retrieved by its ID. The POST operation initializes the todo resource required for retrieval.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item for the authenticated user by inserting a record into the todo_list_todos table. The request must include a non-empty, maximum 255-character title, with an optional description up to 1000 characters. The completed status is always false at creation, in accordance with the business requirement for strict user data privacy and essential workflow. The owning user is identified from the JWT/session context, guaranteeing ownership isolation. System-managed fields such as id, ownerId, createdAt, updatedAt, and completedAt are handled automatically; only the user-provided title and optional description are accepted in the request body. The response returns the newly created todo, including all fields as stored.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user.

This operation allows a logged-in user to add a new personal todo. The mandatory title field must be a non-blank string between 1 and 255 characters and will be trimmed of whitespace; if a description is supplied, it can be up to 1000 characters after trimming. Ownership is enforced by associating the todo with the user making the request, and all system-managed fields (id, completed, timestamps) will be set automatically.

Security is provided by requiring authentication and storing the ownerId based on the session. User input is validated for maximum lengths and required fields. No cross-user access or multi-user features are permitted—the operation strictly ensures that only the authenticated user's todo items are created and accessible.

All validation errors or unauthorized access attempts yield clear business-level error messages with no technical details. Deletion, viewing, or editing of todos outside of authenticated personal scope is never possible via this endpoint.
operations.summary: Create a new todo in todo_list_todos for the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Data for creating a new todo, including required title (1-255 chars) and optional description (up to 1000 chars, both trimmed). Ownership is assigned by the system.

responseBody.description: Created todo item including all system-managed and user-supplied fields.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo item—identified by its UUID—owned by the authenticated user in the todo_list_todos table. The request supports changing the title (non-empty, max 255 chars), optional description (max 1000 chars), and the completed boolean status. The system automatically manages updatedAt timestamps and updates completedAt when the completed status changes. Ownership is strictly enforced: only the creator of the todo may update it, and attempts to edit others' todos are denied. All system-managed fields other than those updatable via this operation remain immutable via the API. Responses return the updated todo in full detail as stored in the database.
operations.description:
Update a todo item belonging to the authenticated user by UUID.

This operation allows a user to edit their own todo's title, description, and completed status. Title and description are validated using the same rules as creation (trimmed, 1-255 for title, <=1000 for description). Changing the completed flag sets or clears the completedAt field automatically. Security and privacy are strictly maintained: only the owning user may perform updates, and attempts to interact with others' data are rejected.

System-managed fields not applicable to client updates (such as id, ownerId, createdAt) cannot be changed by the user. Error scenarios, such as not-found or unauthorized access, return business-context error messages only. All update logic is atomic, ensuring that partial changes never occur under normal operation.
operations.summary: Update a todo in todo_list_todos by UUID for the authenticated user.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item to update. Must be a valid UUID owned by the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Data to update the todo item. Supports changes to title (1-255 chars), description (up to 1000 chars), and completed status.

responseBody.description: The updated todo item with all current fields populated.

operations.name: update

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a specific todo item from the system. It operates on the todo_list_todos table as defined in the Prisma schema. The endpoint is designed so that any authenticated user can remove a todo item they own, and the identifier in the path must correspond to an existing todo record. The operation fully removes the record from the user's list, ensuring it will no longer appear in queries or user interfaces.

The primary use case supported by this API is user-initiated removal of personal todo items. Deletion is handled as a hard delete: the record is completely removed from the database, and no further reference to this item remains after the operation succeeds. Security logic should guarantee that users may only erase items they own unless administrative override logic is implemented elsewhere.

This operation is part of the core todo management functionality, complementing other endpoints for creation, retrieval, and update of todo items. Error handling must address cases where the todoId path parameter does not correspond to an existing item, or when access is denied due to insufficient permissions. No request body is required; only the identifier in the path is needed.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a todo item with the specified identifier from the database.

This API operation allows an authenticated user to delete a todo item from their todo list. Once deleted, the item is fully removed from the system and cannot be recovered. The operation validates that the todoId exists and that the requester has permission to perform this action.

Security checks are enforced to ensure users may only delete their own todo items. The operation handles error situations such as missing or invalid identifiers, or attempts to delete items the user does not own. This endpoint does not accept a request body and relies solely on the identifier specified in the path.

This hard delete complements other CRUD functionality for todo items, enabling users to maintain and curate their own lists. Subsequent list queries will not return any deleted items.
operations.summary: Delete a specific todo item by its identifier from todo_list_todos.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo item to be deleted.

operations.name: erase

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoListUser.IJoin.description:
Registration request DTO for creating a new user account.

This schema is used when a new individual registers for the Todo List application. It represents only the fields allowed for self-registration: a unique email address and a password. No additional personal data, actor role, or administrative flags are accepted or permitted.

This DTO requires that the email be unique in the todo_list_users table and conform to a valid email format. The password is received in plain text here (per security requirements), and will be hashed by the backend before persisting to the password_hash field in the database, never stored as plain text.

Session context fields (href, referrer, ip) are required to support audit trails, security, and compliance. These values are logged in the session table as part of the initial session creation. All session context fields (href, referrer) must be included in the request by the client, and ip may be provided or omitted as the backend can extract it from the network connection.

No userId or identity fields may be specified here—the server will generate those.

Edge cases: rejection on duplicate email, invalid email, or weak password. See requirements for additional constraints.

email.description: Email address of the registering user. Must be unique across all users in the todo_list_users table. Used as the only login credential.

password.description: Plaintext password submitted by the user during registration. Will be hashed server-side before storage in password_hash. Minimum 8, maximum 72 characters. Must meet password policy requirements.

href.description: The exact URL or route at which registration was performed (required for session context tracking, audit, and security compliance). Provided by client.

referrer.description: The referrer URL or previous page, provided by client as required context for session record creation and audit trail.

ip.description: Public IP address from which registration is initiated. Optional (client may provide, or backend extracts from connection). Nullable. Used for session audit.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response payload for successful Todo List user authentication, either via login or token refresh. Conforms to the IAuthorized contract.

Returns the user ID, primary JWT access and refresh tokens, and session auditing data. The token field references the IAuthorizationToken schema with detailed token structure. This object must never include any password, hash, session secret, or raw credential field in any context.

email.description: Email address of the authenticated user. Used as the actor principal for all business operations.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created. Immutable and managed by the system; never user-supplied. Formatted as ISO 8601 date-time string.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated user. Corresponds to the primary key in the 'todo_list_users' table.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
User login credentials for authenticating an existing Todo List user via email and password.

This schema collects the minimum set of credential data to validate access to the system: the user's email and a plain-text password. The operation checks existence of the email and verifies the supplied password for access, referencing the 'todo_list_users' table and its canonical authentication flow.

This operation is strictly for self-login. No extra fields, user IDs, or session tokens are permitted in this request. All additional session context (ip, href, referrer) must also be collected, respecting the session-table pattern for device/audit trail. All fields are mandatory except ip, which is optional for SSR/backend extraction. Never include password hashes or user/session IDs in this DTO; only these fields are provided by the client.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and primary identification. Must exist in the 'todo_list_users' table and is used as the business identifier for user lookup and credential validation. Validated per RFC 5322 email format.

password.description: Plain text password to verify credentials for the given email. Subject to strong password requirements as described in business rules. This value is never persisted; only 'password_hash' is stored.

oneOf.description: Client's IP address for security audit trail and session tracking. Typically set by the infrastructure or backend (SSR); optional in client requests, null if omitted.
Client's IP address (IPv6) for extended audit capability.
Null if client IP is not available or is provided by backend.

ip.description: Client's IP address for security audit trail and session tracking. Optional; should be left null if not available on the client side. Server may populate this based on request origin. Used in the 'todo_list_user_sessions' table.

href.description: Full absolute URL on which this authentication request was initiated. Used to populate the session record for business auditability. Required and must be set by client (cannot be inferred by backend). Stored in corresponding 'href' session field.

referrer.description: Referrer URL for where the login attempt originated. Used for session tracking and auditing. Required for all self-login cases; may be empty if the login page was directly accessed. Stored in 'referrer' field of the session table.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Token refresh request payload for Todo List user sessions.

This DTO is submitted when the client attempts to exchange an unexpired, valid refresh token for a fresh set of authentication tokens. No other parameters or identifying data are required; authentication occurs entirely based on the refresh token provided per secure HTTP-only cookie or transport policy. The implementation should never accept user IDs, emails, or passwords. This schema matches the atomic contract for secure token refresh flows.

ITodoListUser.ILogout.description:
Session termination confirmation payload for logging out a user.

Returned by the logout endpoint when a user's session in todo_list_user_sessions is invalidated. No actual data is returned beyond confirmation; structure exists to ensure consistent API typing and possible future extension.

Indicates the session for the authenticated user was successfully ended, all access and refresh tokens revoked, and 'expired_at' set in the user session record.

ITodoListUser.description:
Represents a registered user's account profile for the minimal todo list application.

Returned on authenticated profile fetch and after profile updates. Contains user's email and account creation date, but omits sensitive credential fields for security.

All fields are required for valid account identification; business logic ensures strict uniqueness of email and immutability of account creation timestamp.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication and account identification. Must conform to RFC 5322 and be unique for each user.

created_at.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created. Immutable and managed by the system; never user-supplied. Formatted as ISO 8601 date-time string.

email.description: The user's new email address. Must be unique among all user accounts and match the system's email format validation rules. If provided, this replaces the user's current email. Email serves as the business identifier for authentication.

password.description: New plain text password for the account. If provided, it will be hashed and securely stored. Must be strong per security standards: minimum 8 characters, no whitespace trimming, not previously used passwords. This field replaces the existing credential on update.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
User profile update request.

Enables a user to update their account credentials, such as their email or password.
Only fields present in the request are changed—leaving them blank makes no modifications. Email updates must remain unique in the system; password updates follow best security practices and are stored as a hash. The user context is determined by authentication and is not supplied here.

q.description: General search query for IP, href, or referrer substring matching across all the user's sessions. Optional for ad hoc text filtering.

active_only.description: Filter to include only active (not expired) sessions. When true, only currently valid sessions are listed. When false or omitted, both active and expired sessions are included.

ip.description: Filter to include only sessions origined from this specific IP address. Optional; useful for per-location or per-device queries.

href.description: Sessions starting at this specific URL (exact match). Optional; restricts list to sessions initiated by particular pages.

referrer.description: Sessions that were created with this referrer URL. Allows filtering by link/referral source. Optional.

created_from.description: Start of the creation date filter range (inclusive, ISO8601). Only sessions created at or after this timestamp are included. Optional.

created_to.description: End of the creation date filter range (inclusive, ISO8601). Only sessions created at or before this timestamp are included. Optional.

expired_from.description: Start of the expiry date filter range (inclusive, ISO8601). Only sessions expired at or after this timestamp are included. Optional.

expired_to.description: End of the expiry date filter range (inclusive, ISO8601). Only sessions expired at or before this timestamp are included. Optional.

page.description: Page number of results to return (for pagination). Defaults to 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Maximum number of session summary records to return per page. Defaults to system configuration (typically 20-50). May not exceed 100.

oneOf.description: Field by which to sort results. Allowed values are 'created_at' and 'expired_at'.
Field by which to sort results. Allowed values are 'created_at' and 'expired_at'.

sort_by.description: Field by which to sort results. Allowed values are 'created_at' and 'expired_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort order: 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.
Sort order: 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.

order.description: Sort order: 'asc' for ascending or 'desc' for descending.

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Session search, filter, and pagination request body for authenticated user's session records.

Supports audit, privacy review, and management of user sessions by allowing filtering by status, IP, originating URLs, referrer, time ranges, and basic text queries. Enables advanced pagination and sorting across all the user's recorded session data. All criteria are optional; absence of filters returns all sessions for the actor.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Session record for a user login in the minimal Todo List application.

Represents a single point-in-time authenticated session for a specific user. Each session is established during successful login and includes audit metadata such as IP address, referrer, session creation and expiration times. Users may have multiple concurrent sessions for multi-device access, and session termination (logout or expiration) is modeled via the 'expired_at' field.

This schema contains only publicly auditable session data (no tokens or sensitive authentication fields) and follows strict privacy and access control rules, allowing users to review their own session records for transparency. All fields mirror those in the underlying Prisma model.

id.description: Unique session identifier (UUID). Serves as the primary key and correlates to a single login event. Used for session lookups, auditing, and invalidation.

ip.description: IP address of the device from which the session originated. This value is recorded for each session and is used for audit, analytics, and suspicious login detection.

href.description: Full URL at which the session was established. Captured at login time to provide an audit trail and for debugging session issues.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the page from where login occurred or the preceding navigation step. Used for analytics and session source tracking.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created (ISO 8601 format).

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired or was invalidated (ISO 8601). May be null if session is still active.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Query/search parameters for listing or filtering a user's todo items.

Defines valid fields and filters for the Todo List search operation, enabling clients to fetch, sort, and filter their own todos with fine granularity. Includes pagination (limit, page), sorting (order), and business-specific filters such as completion status or keyword text search. This schema enables highly controlled access to private per-user task data, and only allows the authenticated user to query their own records.

No user ID filter is supported by business logic—all requests are strictly scoped to authenticated user's records. Any field not defined here will be rejected at API layer.

page.description: Page number for paginated queries. First page is 1. If omitted, defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per page. Upper bound is 100 to control payload size.

completed.description: If provided, filters for todos that match completion status: true for completed, false for not completed. When omitted, results include both states.

search.description: Free-text search term applied to todo item titles (and optionally descriptions or content). Enables case-insensitive, partial-match searching limited to the authenticated user's own tasks.

oneOf.description: Field to sort results by. Supports creation, last modification, or completion timestamp for flexible user-facing task ordering.
Field to sort results by. Supports creation, last modification, or completion timestamp for flexible user-facing task ordering.
Field to sort results by. Supports creation, last modification, or completion timestamp for flexible user-facing task ordering.

sort_by.description: Field to sort results by. Supports creation, last modification, or completion timestamp for flexible user-facing task ordering.

oneOf.description: Sort direction: ascending or descending. Used in conjunction with 'sort_by' field to direct result ordering.
Sort direction: ascending or descending. Used in conjunction with 'sort_by' field to direct result ordering.

order.description: Sort direction: ascending or descending. Used in conjunction with 'sort_by' field to direct result ordering.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Detailed record for a single Todo item owned by a user.

This schema models the complete database structure and business-relevant fields for per-user todo items in the application, enforcing strict user ownership and privacy. The 'id' is the immutable, globally unique identifier for this todo; 'user_id' establishes ownership and always refers to a valid user in the users table, but is never populated in API responses for privacy-preserving design.

The primary business fields are 'title' (required short label), optional 'description', boolean 'completed' status (defaults to false), and nullable 'completed_at' timestamp for when and only when the item is marked complete. Audit fields 'created_at' and 'updated_at' allow sorting, filtering, and audit-trail features. All validation, limits, and nullability reflect both the business requirements and the Prisma schema column constraints.

id.description: Permanent, globally unique identifier for this todo item. Automatically generated by the database. Used for queries, updates, and all item associations within the user's collection.

title.description: Required, user-defined short label. Must be a non-empty string of maximum 255 characters. Used as the primary display name for the todo.

oneOf.description: Optional user-supplied details for this todo item (up to 1000 characters). Can be null if no detail is needed.

description.description: Optional, possibly null, human-readable note field. Used for a longer description or additional context. Null means 'not supplied'.

completed.description: Whether the todo has been marked as complete. Always false initially, set true only by the user.

oneOf.description: Timestamp of when the todo was completed (ISO8601). Set only if and when marked as complete, otherwise null.

completed_at.description: The date/time when todo was marked completed. Null if not completed. Populated only upon changing 'completed' from false to true.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the todo was first created (UTC, ISO8601). Used for audit trails and chronological displays.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for when the todo was last modified (UTC, ISO8601). Changes on every edit, including marking completed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. This UUID is generated as the primary key in the database and is used to locate and reference the todo.

title.description: Short label for the todo item, defined by the user. Maximum 255 characters. Required and used for list display and main identification, as enforced by the database constraint.

completed.description: Completion status for the todo. Set true if the task is finished, false otherwise. Defaults to false on creation and always reflects user action.

created_at.description: Timestamp of when the todo item was created. Used for audit, ordering, and transparency. Always set, never nullable.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to the todo item. Reflects the last time any property was modified.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a todo item record for list or lightweight usage.

Includes only essential and compact fields required for listing, search, and quick reference, not detailed/optional/task progress fields.

Omits user reference, description, and completion timestamp for list performance and privacy. Used in result sets and bulk display operations.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Data required to create a new todo item as an authenticated user.

The write request body consists of business fields only; actor fields (user identity, id, created_at, updated_at, completed, completed_at) are all system-managed and must not appear here. The server populates mandatory ownership and audit fields automatically from session context.

A valid request requires a non-empty string 'title' (trimmed, 1-255 chars), and can supply an optional 'description' up to 1000 characters, or null. Validation and length constraints strictly match the database. All other fields are excluded and system-managed.

title.description: Required todo short label. Must be a non-empty string trimmed of whitespace, up to 255 characters. This value is the main identifying field for the new todo.

oneOf.description: Optional expanded user-provided context for the todo (up to 1000 chars after trimming).

description.description: Optional, nullable free-form field for additional context. If absent or null, no description is stored. Max length is 1000 characters.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating a todo item. Allows updating of the business fields 'title', 'description', and 'completed' via partial update semantics (PATCH/PUT).

All properties are optional; any subset of fields may be provided in a given update request, and properties omitted will not be changed. System-managed fields and user ownership cannot be mutated via this DTO. Only the authenticated owner of the target todo may issue an update.

Validation rules and length constraints match the creation contract and database schema: 'title' (if supplied) must be trimmed, 1–255 characters; 'description' (if supplied) must not exceed 1000 characters or may be explicitly set to null to clear it; 'completed' is a boolean status flag which, when changed, updates the backend audit timestamp and completion status accordingly.

title.description:
Short user-defined label for the todo item. Trimmed and between 1 and 255 characters in length as per the database schema. May be omitted for partial field update.

If supplied, this field will update the display label for the todo item. The value must be a non-empty string, trimmed of leading and trailing whitespace. Used as the primary identifying field for both creation and update operations.

oneOf.description: Optional, user-supplied descriptive text for the todo item, up to 1000 characters. Can be set to null to explicitly clear any existing description from the record.

description.description: Optional, possibly null, free-form text field. Supplies additional business context or clarifies the task. If set to null, the backend will blank or remove the stored description.

completed.description:
Boolean status flag. Set to true if the todo item is completed, or false to mark it as not yet completed. Updating this flag triggers automatic audit updates in the database.

Changing this flag will update the 'completed_at' timestamp and reflect completion status in various user interfaces and backend reports.

id.description: Unique identifier for this user session. Generated by the system, referenced in session tracking and audit operations.

ip.description: The IP address from which this session was initiated, as recorded in the session tracking table. Used for audit and suspicious login detection.

href.description: The exact URL where the login session originated, captured for audit transparency.

referrer.description: Referrer URL indicating the previous page or external context from which the session started, or the login screen URL if direct access.

created_at.description: Timestamp specifying when the session was created. Used in audit trails and session expiration logic.

oneOf.description: Timestamp setting when a session was explicitly expired or invalidated. Null if the session is still active.
Null value when the session is active and not yet expired.

expired_at.description: Timestamp or null for session expiration. Set automatically by the system upon session invalidation or logout actions.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for a todo list user session. Includes essential session tracking data fields required for session list views and auditing but omits user reference information for privacy.
